main_text.p: mirum, quòd vna tantùm eadémque fim-pliciffima in auguftiffimo illo Trinitatis myfterio communis effentia reperiatur, quæ totam in fe deitatis continet perfe-ctionem: tres verò proprietates perfonales, quibus tres perfonæ conftituuntur ac inter fefe diftinguuntur.

Prima f. lib. 2. c. 12. &c.8 Veruntamen fanctiffimæ Trinitatis facramentum plane eft incomparabile, adeóque rerum naturam, omnémque mentis humanæ, imò & angelicæ capacitatem in immenfum excedit, in eo, quòd effentia illa in tribus diuinis perfonis fub fiftens, non fpecie aut fola ratione, vna, ficut in creaturis vfuuenit, fed vna fit penitus atque fimpliciffima.

9 Hinc & illud fit perfpicuum, aliud effe, quædam in vnam eandémque naturam vniri, aliud verò in perfonæ vnitatem coagmentari. Illa fiquidem in natura dicimus vnita, quæ in vna conueniunt οὐσία, fiue id fiat abfque vlla concretione, miftione aut conuerfione, vt in diuinis perfonis inuenitur: fiue fola compofitione, vt in hominis ex anima & corpore conftitutione: fiue denique intercedente mixtione aliqua, confufione aut conuerfione, vt in elementorum tranfmutatione &

page.notes: The Greek word "οὐσία" is printed in Greek letters. The left-margin reference is small and partly faded; "Prima f. lib. 2." is read with some uncertainty. The bottom line of the text is partly cut off at the foot of the page and is read as "ne &".
